items.title: Mahalanobis pseudometric induced by a positive-semidefinite matrix

references.title: Kilian Q. Weinberger and Lawrence K. Saul, Distance Metric Learning for Large Margin Nearest Neighbor Classification, JMLR 10 (2009), 207–244
Aurélien Bellet, Amaury Habrard, and Marc Sebban, A Survey on Metric Learning for Feature Vectors and Structured Data, arXiv:1306.6709v4 (2014)

items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. A real matrix $M\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is positive semidefinite, written $M\succeq0$, when it is symmetric and $v^{T}Mv\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$. For $x,x'\in\mathbb R^d$, define the squared Mahalanobis distance and its nonnegative square root by

$$q_M(x,x') := (x-x')^{T}M(x-x'),\qquad d_M(x,x') := \sqrt{q_M(x,x')}.$$

The square root is defined because $q_M(x,x')\ge0$. A pseudometric is a nonnegative symmetric function that vanishes on the diagonal and satisfies the triangle inequality, but may assign distance zero to distinct points. The function $d_M$ is called the Mahalanobis pseudometric associated with $M$; $q_M=d_M^2$ is its squared-distance form. The theorem on this page proves the pseudometric properties and the equivalent linear-feature representation.

items.title: Symmetric matrices are Euclidean under the Frobenius norm

references.title: Nicholas J. Higham, Computing a Nearest Symmetric Positive Semidefinite Matrix, Linear Algebra and its Applications 103 (1988), 103–118
David Bindel, Matrix Computations, CS 6210, Matrix Nearness Problems, Fall 2022

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$, let $\mathbb S^d$ be the real vector space of symmetric $d\times d$ matrices, and set $m=d(d+1)/2$. Equip $\mathbb S^d$ with the Frobenius inner product $\langle A,B\rangle_F:=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d}A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and its induced norm. Define $\operatorname{svec}:\mathbb S^d\to\mathbb R^m$ by listing $A_{11},\ldots,A_{dd}$ first, followed by $\sqrt2 A_{ij}$ for $1\le i<j\le d$ in lexicographic order. Then $\operatorname{svec}$ is a linear bijection and preserves inner products and norms; in particular, $\|\operatorname{svec}(A)-\operatorname{svec}(B)\|_2=\|A-B\|_F$ for all $A,B\in\mathbb S^d$.

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$ and let $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be symmetric. There exists an orthogonal eigendecomposition $A=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)U^T$. For any such decomposition define $\lambda_i^+=\max\{\lambda_i,0\}$ and $A_+=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1^+,\ldots,\lambda_d^+)U^T$. Let $\mathbb S_+^d$ be the set of real symmetric matrices $Z$ with $v^TZv\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\|B\|_F=(\sum_{i,j}B_{ij}^2)^{1/2}$. Then $A_+$ is the unique minimizer of $\|A-Z\|_F$ over $Z\in\mathbb S_+^d$, so its value is independent of the chosen orthogonal eigendecomposition.

items.title: The real positive-semidefinite cone is closed in the Frobenius metric

references.title: Nicholas J. Higham, Computing a Nearest Symmetric Positive Semidefinite Matrix, Linear Algebra and its Applications 103 (1988), 103–118
David Bindel, Matrix Computations, CS 6210, Matrix Nearness Problems, Fall 2022

items.statement: For an integer $d\ge1$, let $\mathbb S^d$ be the real symmetric $d\times d$ matrices and let $\mathbb S_+^d=\{M\in\mathbb S^d:v^TMv\ge0\text{ for every }v\in\mathbb R^d\}$. With the Frobenius norm $\|A\|_F=(\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}^2)^{1/2}$, the set $\mathbb S_+^d$ is closed in $\mathbb S^d$.

items.statement: Let $d\ge1$ and let $M\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be real symmetric and positive semidefinite, meaning $v^TMv\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$. Define $q_M(x,x')=(x-x')^TM(x-x')$ and $d_M(x,x')=\sqrt{q_M(x,x')}$. Then there is a real matrix $L\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ with $M=L^TL$ and, for all $x,x'\in\mathbb R^d$, $d_M(x,x')=\|Lx-Lx'\|_2$. Consequently $d_M$ is nonnegative, symmetric, zero on the diagonal, and satisfies the triangle inequality, without asserting separation of distinct points.

items.title: LMNN hinge subgradient formula and a uniform data-dependent bound

references.title: Kilian Q. Weinberger and Lawrence K. Saul, Distance Metric Learning for Large Margin Nearest Neighbor Classification, JMLR 10 (2009), 207–244
Sébastien Bubeck, Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity, Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 8(3–4) (2015)
Dimitri P. Bertsekas, Convex Analysis and Optimization, MIT 6.253 Complete Lecture Notes

items.statement:
Fix the finite labeled sample, fixed target sets, and $\mu\in[0,1]$ of the LMNN objective. For each $j\in N_i$ and each impostor index $l$ with $y_l\ne y_i$, set $C_{ij}=(x_i-x_j)(x_i-x_j)^T$, $D_{ijl}=C_{ij}-C_{il}$, and $h_{ijl}(M)=1+\langle M,D_{ijl}\rangle_F$, where $\langle A,B\rangle_F=\sum_{r,s}A_{rs}B_{rs}$. Define $\gamma_{ijl}(M)=1$ if $h_{ijl}(M)>0$ and $\gamma_{ijl}(M)=0$ if $h_{ijl}(M)\le0$. Put

$$G(M)=(1-\mu)\sum_i\sum_{j\in N_i}C_{ij}+\mu\sum_i\sum_{j\in N_i}\sum_{l:y_l\ne y_i}\gamma_{ijl}(M)D_{ijl}.$$

For the convex objective $F_\mu$ on $\mathbb S_+^d$, a Frobenius subgradient at $M$ means a symmetric matrix $G$ such that $F_\mu(N)\ge F_\mu(M)+\langle G,N-M\rangle_F$ for every $N\in\mathbb S_+^d$. Then $G(M)$ is a subgradient at every $M\in\mathbb S_+^d$. Moreover, uniformly in $M$,

$$\|G(M)\|_F\le B_{\rm data}:=(1-\mu)\sum_i\sum_{j\in N_i}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2+\mu\sum_i\sum_{j\in N_i}\sum_{l:y_l\ne y_i}\bigl(\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2+\|x_i-x_l\|_2^2\bigr).$$

At an exact hinge kink $h_{ijl}(M)=0$, the selected subgradient coefficient is $0$.
